messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

Given the following text and a relational triplet extracted from it:

Text: The most important interactions with spironolactone are medicines that also raise potassium.
The combined effect of these medicines can push your potassium level dangerously high.
Tell your doctor about every medicine you take, including anything you start or stop during treatment.
Be especially careful with:
eplerenone, which should not be taken with spironolactone at all;
medicines that raise potassium, including ACE inhibitors such as lisinopril and ramipril, ARBs such as losartan and valsartan, NSAIDs, heparin and low molecular weight heparin, and trimethoprim;
potassium supplements and potassium-containing salt substitutes, which are usually stopped when spironolactone is started for heart failure;
Spironolactone slows how fast your kidneys clear spironolactone.
Spironolactone can cause lithium toxicity.
Lithium levels need monitoring.
Digoxin needs care for two separate reasons.
Spironolactone interferes with one type of blood test used to measure digoxin.
Spironolactone can raise the actual amount of digoxin in your body.
Triplet: ["spironolactone", "has effect on drug level", "can raise actual amount of digoxin in your body"]

The relation 'has effect on drug level' in the triplet is defined as 'The subject drug can alter the concentration or effectiveness of the drug specified by the object entity in the body.' In this context, is there any relation appropriate to replace it? Choose a relation whose meaning and subject/object direction match the triplet even if the wording differs; choose 'None of the above' only if no candidate fits. Please answer by providing only the letter of your choice.

Choices:
A. 'has effect': The subject drug produces the effect specified by the object entity.
B. 'acts in': The subject drug exerts its effects within the anatomical or physiological system specified by the object entity.
C. 'dose adjustment responsibility': The entity specified by the object is responsible for making changes to the dose of the subject drug.
D. 'interacts with': The subject drug has a drug interaction with the drug or substance specified by the object entity that may change effects or cause harm.
E. 'improves': The subject drug enhances or positively affects the condition or parameter specified by the object entity.
F. None of the above.
